newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's oil field bids beating expectations.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's oil field bids beating expectations.

text.p: The first two bids during the first day of Venezuela's third oil contracts auction round have beaten expectations and augur well for the rest of the week, Venezuelan state oil company PDVSA President Luis Giusti said.
"Of course there 18 more areas (to sell) and a lot of these are bigger and richer than those we saw this morning," Giusti told reporters in between auctions.
"This is looking very good for the rest of the week."

A wave of ohhs and whistles rose from the audience when a domestic consortium that grouped Cosa Ingenieros Consultores, Cartera de Inversiones Venezolanas CA and Phoenix International CA offered a winning $27.58 million bid for Venezuela's Casma- Anaco oil field, which has 29 million barrels of proven reserves.

Their bid followed a successful $60 million offer earlier Monday morning for the Kaki marginal oil field by a consortium 56 percent owned by U.S. oil company Atlantic Richfield. Kaki has 135 million barrels of proven reserves.
"Under this opening process, we are tapping all the opportunities, we are enlarging our portfolio and it's looking very nice," Giusti added.

The two fields were the first to be sold among the five Monday reserved for consortia with at least 30 percent Venezuelan participation. Three more are to be auctioned this afternoon: Mata, with 101 million barrels of proven reserves (1400 local/1800 GMT); Maulpa with 119 million barrels (1600 local/2000 GMT); and Acema with 33 million (1800 local/2200 GMT).
Under the third auction round, which continues through the week, a total of 131 companies are competing for 20 contracts with the winners determined purely by the size of their bids.
Under 20-year contracts, the operator produces hydrocarbons on behalf of PDVSA subsidiary Corpoven in exchange for a fee worked out on a sliding scale.
